Duck-Fat Roasted Baby Potatoes

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 45 min

Duck-Fat Roasted Baby Potatoes are a rich and flavorful side dish traditionally served at the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet. This feast commemorates the innocent children lost, and the dish's comforting warmth symbolizes care and remembrance during the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900 g) baby potatoes, halved if large
  • 3 tablespoons (45 ml) duck fat
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) kosher salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) freshly ground black pepper
  • 2 teaspoons (2 g) fresh rosemary, chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) fresh parsley, chopped (optional, for garnish)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. In a large bowl, toss the baby potatoes with the duck fat, kosher salt, black pepper, rosemary, and minced garlic until evenly coated.
  3. Spread the potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or a roasting pan.
  4. Roast in the preheated oven for 40-45 minutes, turning the potatoes halfway through, until they are golden brown and crispy on the outside and tender inside.
  5. Remove from the oven and sprinkle with fresh parsley if desired before serving.

Tips

  • For extra crispiness, parboil the potatoes for 5 minutes before roasting and drain well.
  • If duck fat is unavailable, use goose fat or a high-quality olive oil as a substitute, though the flavor will differ.
  • Add a pinch of smoked paprika or a squeeze of lemon juice after roasting for a flavor twist.
